summary.text: Belinda Stojcevski is the Liberal candidate for Thomastown at the 2026 Victorian election. A small business owner from Lalor, she has owned hairdressing salons since the age of 21. Her party page says she wants infrastructure and services to keep up with the area's growth.

priorities.text: Better local services and infrastructure that keeps pace with growth
More help for people who are being left behind

summary.text: Bronwyn Halfpenny has represented Thomastown for Labor in the Legislative Assembly since 2010. Before that she was an official of the manufacturing workers' union and worked at the Victorian Trades Hall Council. In Parliament she has been government whip, an acting speaker and parliamentary secretary for several portfolios, most recently the State Electricity Commission. She is running again in Thomastown at the 2026 election.

summary.text: Gavin Trewella is the Greens candidate for Thomastown at the 2026 Victorian election. A field ecologist and researcher who holds a Charles Darwin University doctorate in wildlife management, he does casual work for an environmental consultancy on building projects across Melbourne. He says he has lived in Thomastown for most of his life.

occupation.text: Field ecologist and researcher (casual, environmental consultancy)

priorities.text: I'm running to revitalize the outer north
Public grocery stores, cutting stamp duty, rent caps and building public housing
Returning energy supply to public ownership
Funding for arts, culture and environmental projects

summary.text: Nadia Anthony is One Nation's candidate for Thomastown at the 2026 Victorian election. A counsellor by occupation, she moved from Mauritius to study in 2007, the ABC reports; she says her counselling has included people out of work and from many cultures, and that she takes part in church and community life locally. One Nation's candidate page could not be read for this profile.

sources.title: Thomastown: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Priya Reddy is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Thomastown at the 2026 Victorian election. She works as a veterinary nurse while studying to become a teacher, and says she grew up in the area's culturally diverse community as the child of Indo-Fijian migrants. She has campaigned on Palestine, refugee rights and environmental issues.

priorities.text: More funding for the Northern Hospital and better conditions for its staff
Opposing the planned waste incinerator at Wollert
Fully funded public schools and better working conditions for teachers
Spending on health, education and housing rather than weapons

summary.text: Rob Rancie (spelt Ranchie in the ABC's guide) is the Family First candidate for Thomastown at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. His party page says he founded a financial planning firm in Bendigo more than 40 years ago, now run by his sons from Melbourne, after starting out as a secondary teacher with an economics degree. He and his wife raised ten children, and he spent four years doing charity work in China.
